You can achieve a maximum of 315% with melee prowess, enduring strike, and the dual effect mods. There are 3 slots open status chance mods achieving a max status multiplier of 180%. EB base status chance is 10%. so you get at most 28% status chance.

In statistics, chance of critting via DE's naive RNG method has something similar to IID, independent and identically distributed random variable. that means every strike has it's own random variable and doesn't effect the chance of future strikes critting/procing. (assuming perfect RNG, which it isn't). This gives berserker an innate advantage

Crit with Berserker allows you to increase your attack speed everytime you crit. meaning you'll be outputting more strikes. each strike procs it's own crit/status. Therefore more strikes = higher overall chance (Since chances are additive here). You can replace a status mods (shocking and fevering) for berserker. (you have 15% chance per strike, high base speed = higher chance) replace the left over status mod with a dual status mod.

I think fighting ability denotes their capability to deal with the number and level of threats. The all-machine character can deploy all over the city and handle multiple threats all at once, so he scores 10, and the telekinetic character can obviously influence multiple threats. 9 is probably the maximum for people who can't influence entire cities. The mysterious hero's achievements are based on multiple dragon level threats which is probably why he got 10.

The series is suffering from classic data manipulation flaw:

1) they're narrowing the range on the stats (the cyborg hero counted up to 15 which is a higher range to account for anomalies like the protagonist), so comparisons can't be accurate

2) the fields are not atomic (if my fighting ability interpretation is correct, then fighting ability can be separated into 2 more fields: ability to deal with threat level, and influence area [speedsters, telekinetic, mechanics would dominate here]). Another example: Endurance/Physical Fitness can be separated into stamina, willpower/pain resistance/tolerance, regeneration, resistance to damage, classic rpg stuff. The zombie-like hero can get max stat for regen and willpower, but low for resistance, and moderate for stamina (he got exhausted after fighting 1 demon level threat for 10 minutes).

3) heterogenous weighting: from the exams, they seem to make Intelligence and Justice weigh 50% of the exam, and all the other stuff (speed, strength, endurance, fighting ability) to the other 50%. instead if they make all atomic variables weigh equally, the ranking system would be slightly more balanced.

I do believe those are called fillers... and for some reason, everyone hates it. I remember first watching animated series and never skipping fillers; I actually enjoyed them. (I'm not defining fillers as non-canon content, but rather as plot fillers that don't really need filling)

Almost all popular shows have these side characters going for them, all animated series follow roughly similar character structure: 

the rival, the bro from another mo with a slight age difference (Genos... another example: Killer B, Naruto/Klein/Agil, SAO a few others... although these relationship aren't as strong as GenosXsaitama), brother from another mother without an age difference (King...), cool chick (Fubuki), angry chick (Tatsumaki), motivator (metal bat), old guy (bang), the hero (licenceless rider), etc.

I would have to disagree and say that One Punch Man season 1 is an excellent gateway to animated series, since it's palpable (only 12 episodes), follows roughly the same structure 90% filler, entertaining fillers (there are quite a few in almost all animated series), same character roles, smooth transition from mainstream ensemble shows like Monty Python, Seinfeld, HIMYM, and Game of Thrones as well as character focused shows that also emphasizes the background like Breaking Bad, Dr. Who, and Batman the animated series.
